The petitioner herein is accused No.1 seeking regular bail in respect of Crime No.36/2023 of Hatcholli Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 376(2)(n), 114 R/W 34 of Indian Penal Code (for short "IPC") and under Sections 5(L), 5(j), 6, 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (for short "POCSO Act").

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
3. Brief facts of the case:-
The complaint is filed by the father of the victim stating that his minor girl aged about 17 years was abducted by the petitioner on the pretext of marriage and committed sexual assault against the victim even though NC: 2023:KHC-D:14705 she is a minor.
Thereby, the petitioner has committed offences as stated supra.
The jurisdictional police have conducted the investigation and submitted charge sheet.
4. It is the submission of learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is innocent of the alleged offences and infact, the petitioner and the victim were loving each other.
They have decided to marry each other.
Due to some difference of opinion between the family members, they have decided to elope and marry.
The petitioner and the victim on 01.06.2023 voluntary left the home and reached Bengaluru by bus and stayed at Bengaluru till 08.06.2023.
They have been secured by the jurisdictional police on 08.06.2023.
The petitioner was arrested on the same day.
5. The petitioner is the permanent resident of Byragamadinni village, Siruguppa taluk.
The petitioner is aged about 21 years and he is a student.
The petitioner will abide the conditions imposed by this Court in the event of his release on bail.

Making such submission, the NC:
2023:KHC-D:14705 learned counsel for the petitioner prays to allow the petition.
6. Per contra, Shri Praveena Y. Devareddiyavara, the learned HCGP vehemently opposed the bail application and submitted that the offence is heinous in nature, which is committed against the minor.

The petitioner herein deliberately abducted the victim and took her to Bengaluru and K Shashikumar S/O K Veeresh vs The State Of Karnataka on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48701771/
2 confined her in a room and committed sexual assault continuously for 8 days and thereafter, they have been secured by the respondent/police.

entities.text: K Shashikumar S/O K Veeresh vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for bail.
If the petitioner is enlarged on bail, there may be chances of absconding or fleeing away from justice.
Making such submission, the learned HCGP prays to dismiss petition.
7. Sri S.G.Kadakatti, learned counsel for the respondent No.2 adopted the said submission and also prays to dismiss the petition by filing the statement of objections.

Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the averments of the charge sheet and also complaint, it appears that the petitioner herein abducted the victim on 01.06.2023 at about 12.30 a.m. from her house and went to Bengaluru.
Both have stayed at Bannerghatta area till 08.06.2023 and said to have committed sexual assault against the victim.
After they have been secured by the jurisdictional police, the petitioner was arrested on the same day.
The victim has been produced before the Magistrate for recording the statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
On 14.06.2023, the victim has stated about the incident before the Magistrate.
However, on 16.06.2023, again she made statement before the police and turned hostile to the earlier statement.
Considering the hostility of the victim, it is appropriate to grant bail by imposing suitable conditions.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.36/2023 of Hatcholli Police Station on executing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One lakh only) with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Trial Court, subject to the following conditions:
a) The petitioner shall not threaten or tamper the prosecution witnesses nor hamper the proceedings of the Court.
b) The petitioner shall appear before the Trial Court on all dates of hearing without fail.
In case, if the petitioner violates any of the bail conditions as stated above, the prosecution will be at liberty to seek for cancellation of bail.
